mechanism: Donepezil (cholinesterase inhibitor) increases acetylcholine levels while tolterodine (anticholinergic) blocks acetylcholine receptors, creating opposing pharmacodynamic effects that may reduce efficacy of both agents.
action: Monitor cognitive function and urinary symptoms closely; consider alternative anticholinergic agents with less CNS penetration or urological alternatives if possible, and ensure benefit-risk ratio justifies concurrent use.
